title: refactor(i18n): retire the 116 dead console.objectView config-panel keys
body:
Refs #4730 — the `console.objectView.*` slice of that umbrella. The umbrella stays open; what remains is listed at the bottom.

Ruled 2026-08-19, option (b): the `console.objectView.*` confirmed-dead keys are deleted under #4658's evidence standard. Maintainer, via the 27-card decision-inbox review, verbatim: 「全部接受」.

## What changed

116 keys removed from each of the ten packs — 1160 translated strings — plus a negative pin and a changeset. The namespace held 209 keys per pack; 93 survive.

The 116 labelled a view-configuration settings panel that does not exist: appearance and density toggles, accessibility attributes, conditional-formatting rules, row-action and inline-edit switches, quick-filter builders, an advanced-settings tier. `packages/app-shell/src/views/ViewConfigPanel.tsx` — the panel they were written for — was migrated off the legacy `buildViewConfigSchema` engine onto `ViewVariantInspector`, a spec-driven inspector whose field labels come from `@objectstack/spec` metadata (through `useMetadataLocale`) rather than from this namespace. The panel was replaced; the keys were not cleaned up with it. That is leg three of the evidence standard, and it is the leg that says *why* rather than *how many*.

Four retired keys name `ListViewSchema` properties that are still active — `rowActions`, `inlineEdit`, `hiddenFields`, `filterableFields`. They are retired anyway, by the ruling's own words: **a live schema property is not a consumer of a locale string; only a labelled UI control is.** Nothing renders a label for them, so nothing reads their label.

## The count, measured on this branch's merge base — not inherited from the card

The card's numbers were ~9 days stale, so the list was re-derived rather than copied.

| | card (2026-08-15) | this branch (merge base `11d3ab999`) |
|---|---|---|
| pack keys (`en`) | 2927 | **2936** |
| referenced keys | 13776 | **14623** |
| `console.objectView` namespace size | 154 | **209** |
| `console.objectView` CONFIRMED | 116 | **116** |
| `console.objectView` NEEDS-REVIEW | 38 | **38** |

The CONFIRMED count landing on 116 again is a coincidence worth naming rather than glossing: the namespace grew by 55 keys in those nine days and every one of them is live or needs-review. The deleted set is the sweep's *current* output, re-run here, not the card's list.

After the deletion: 2820 pack keys, repo-wide CONFIRMED 266 → 150 (−116, exactly the namespace), `console.objectView (0 confirmed, 38 needs-review)`.

## Live/dead split, proved rather than inherited

The 93 survivors are the create-view dialog fields, the view-type catalogue, `new`/`save`/`cancel`, the object-not-found copy, and the 38 NEEDS-REVIEW keys, which are **out of scope here** by the dispatch fence.

**Counter-probed.** A sweep that reports zero because it broke reports the same zero as one that worked, so the zero-footprint claim was run against a known-present control on the identical pipeline. Whole-repo `grep -rFn -I`, everything except the locale packs that define the keys:

- the 116 retired keys → **0 hit lines**
- six live sibling keys (`save`, `new`, `cancel`, `viewTypeGrid`, `viewName`, `configureView`) → **37 hit lines**, every one of the six hitting at least once (1, 19, 2, 6, 8, 1)

## Reverse verification

Direction predicted before running, both legs restored under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`, `git diff HEAD --stat` empty afterwards.

**Leg A — restore one deleted key (`console.objectView.rowActions`, `en` only).** Predicted: sweep CONFIRMED rises by exactly one; the pin goes red; parity goes red. Observed, all three: `150 → 151` with `console.objectView (1 confirmed, 38 needs-review)` naming `console.objectView.rowActions`; the pin red; `all-locales-key-parity` red on the nine other packs.

*First attempt at this leg was mis-anchored and is reported as such:* the anchor `^      save: ` is not unique in `en.ts` and the injection landed in `grid.import`, not `console.objectView`. The sweep still rose 150 → 151, but for `grid.import.rowActions` — a reading about a different namespace, so it was void for the pin and the leg was re-run against the unique anchor `^      cannotDeleteMetaView: `, with the landing site printed (`en.ts:1986`, between `cannotEditMetaView` and `cannotDeleteMetaView`) rather than assumed.

**Leg B — delete one live key (`console.objectView.save`, all ten packs).** This is the counter-probe: it asks whether the live/dead classifier discriminates or passes everything. Predicted: the call-site gate goes red; the pin's live-subset assertion goes red while its retired-key assertions stay green; the sweep does not move. Observed, all four:

- `check-i18n-call-site-keys` **exit 1**, `2548/2549 literal keys resolve` (was 2549/2549), naming `packages/app-shell/src/views/ViewConfigPanel.tsx:302:22  [missing-key]  console.objectView.save`
- the pin: `the retired list is the measured set` ✓, `no pack defines any retired key` ✓, `the namespace root survives…` ×, `the live subset is still a real translation…` ×, `no consuming package asks t() for a retired key` ✓ — 2 failed, 3 passed
- the sweep unchanged at 150 CONFIRMED: a live key removed is not a new candidate

Leg B's on-disk landing proof is the delete script's own per-pack presence assertion (it throws if a target key is absent from any pack), `git diff --numstat` summing to exactly 10 deleted lines across the ten packs, and B1 naming the call site. The value-line `grep` printed alongside it is namespace-blind — `save: 'Save',` occurs twice in `en.ts` — so it is *not* the landing evidence and is not read as such.

## Why a negative pin was added

`packages/i18n/src/__tests__/objectView-config-keys-retired-4730.test.ts` (116 keys by name, following `report-editor-retired-4145.test.ts` next door). This is one file outside the dispatched `locales/**` surface and is called out deliberately.

Every i18n gate in this repo runs **call site → key**, never key → call site. `check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` never visits a key with no call site. `all-locales-key-parity` is *fully satisfied* by 116 dead keys present in all ten packs — that is exactly what it wants. `check-i18n-en-drift.mjs` only fires when an `en` value changes. And `check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs`, the sweep that found these, is report-only by design and wired into no workflow. So nothing here can see this namespace grow back, which is how it grew in the first place. Leg A is that pin firing.

The pin's reader scan is call-shaped and key-specific rather than a substring sweep, the same trade its neighbour makes: this PR's own prose names retired keys, and the 93 live keys in the same namespace must keep working. It asserts its scan roots exist before walking them, because a scan root that silently does not exist walks nothing and passes.

## Gates

Run at `45d434170`, the final commit. Each verdict is the gate's own printed line, with the exit code captured before any pipe.

| gate | exit | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n type-check` | 0 | `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, clean |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/src --maxWorkers=2` (root-form) | 0 | `Test Files 54 passed (54) · Tests 898 passed (898)` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run` — `ViewConfigPanel`, `CreateViewDialog.ariaRequired`, `plugin-view` `ObjectView` ×3 | 0 | `Test Files 5 passed (5) · Tests 57 passed (57)` |
| `pnpm check:i18n-keys` | 0 | `Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (2820 keys)` — 2549/2549 |
| `pnpm check:i18n-drift` | 0 | `0 en value(s) changed (0 key(s) added, 116 removed)` |
| `pnpm check:i18n-dead-keys` | 0 | `console.objectView (0 confirmed, 38 needs-review)` |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | 0 | `OK (scanned 4974 tracked text file(s))` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | `11 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)` |
| `check-changeset-fixed` / `check-changeset-no-major` | 0 / 0 | fixed group OK; no `major` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/i18n lint` | 0 | 0 errors (34 pre-existing warnings elsewhere in the package) |

Lint was **not** narrowed: repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` ran to completion over **3632 files** (the universe read from eslint's own config, the count from its JSON output). It reports 89 errors, all in files this PR does not touch — `apps/console/src/pages/settings/*`, `packages/cli/*`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/*` and others, pre-existing on `main` under the repo's per-package `turbo run lint`. All eleven touched files report **0 errors, 0 warnings**. No type-aware linting is configured (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on a file it does not touch.

CI convergence is the PM's to read; this reports gate state at hand-off, not a wait on CI.

## Not in this PR

The umbrella keeps everything below, so `Refs`, not a closing keyword:

- the **NEEDS-REVIEW tier**, in every namespace, `console.objectView`'s own 38 included — 242/626 of a naive AST-only list would have been wrong without the text safety net, which is this card's own argument for not trusting the AST pass alone
- key-level trims inside *live* namespaces: `search` (measured partially live — 7 `t()` sites in `SearchResultsPage.tsx`), `table`, `report`, `form`, `appDesigner`
- `workflow.*` / `publicForm.demo.*` (→ #4742) and `configPanel.*` / `renderer.*` (→ #4746), already carved out
- `scripts/check-i18n-dead-keys.mjs` is untouched and stays report-only — it is the instrument here, not the target, and `--strict` remains deferred
